article_title: Prediction Versus Explanation in Educational Psychology: a Cross-Theoretical Approach to Using Teacher Behaviour to Predict Student Engagement in Physical Education
citation: Michael Noetel, Philip Parker, Theresa Dicke, Mark R. Beauchamp, Nikos Ntoumanis, Ryan M. Hulteen, et al. (2023). Prediction Versus Explanation in Educational Psychology: a Cross-Theoretical Approach to Using Teacher Behaviour to Predict Student Engagement in Physical Education. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-023-09786-6
title: Catalogue of 71 unique motivational teacher behaviours built via binning and winnowing
description: A reproducible list of teacher behaviours hypothesised by four motivational theories, created through a systematic binning and winnowing protocol. From 111 papers the authors sourced 49 unique scales containing 1151 candidate items, binned them into 61 categories, and winnowed to exemplars, ending with 69 unique behaviours plus two idealised-influence perception items. The article reports "our final list included 71 unique behaviours, 68 related to a psychological need in self-determination theory, 47 of which were characteristic of a leadership style in transformational leadership theory".
requirements: Member checking by author groups and local secondary teachers to identify unclear or redundant behaviours and uncovered motivational behaviours
constraints: Idealised influence of transformational leadership was less conducive to assessment through observable behaviours and was measured as student perception of leader characteristics instead
target_learners: Year 7 secondary school physical education students
target_learning_goals: identifying which teacher behaviours predict change in student engagement
examples: Students rated their teachers on all 71 behaviours on a 7-point Likert scale from Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree
